formal_definition: Not a form of legislation or delegated legislation in its own right, but a supervisory communication issued under a regulator's general supervisory powers, typically grounding its expectations in existing binding requirements -- such as the PRA's Fundamental Rules or Threshold Conditions -- rather than creating new ones. A Dear CEO letter can itself be superseded by a later one on the same subject: the Bank of England PRA's 18 May 2026 letter on deposits, e-money and stablecoins explicitly replaces a predecessor the PRA had issued on the same topic in 2023.
plain_definition: A letter a UK regulator -- most often the Prudential Regulation Authority or the Financial Conduct Authority -- sends to the chief executives of an entire category of regulated firms to set out or clarify its supervisory expectations on a given topic. It does not create new legislation or formal rules; firms are still expected to already meet the underlying obligations, but the letter explains how the regulator expects those obligations to be applied, often in a new or fast-moving area.
